summary: Four findings: three high-severity statement defects and one medium-severity inconsistency in retained proof outlines. The accepted integral Kodaira–Spencer item still identifies a relative Hodge piece with the absolute Cartier-dual Lie module; the test-function item repeats the maximal-compact-to-order inference rejected in E28; a review-added item interchanges the quantifiers on the fields of definition of CM points; several proof outlines still prescribe arguments explicitly rejected by the same review. The first, second and fourth findings concern incomplete propagation of existing corrections, not newly discovered source errata. All 139 items and the nine routes were checked against a complete rereading of the published paper and the revised author erratum. No additional library-claim or ownership finding is asserted.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18.result.json: items[35], PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18/integral-ks.statement; compare sourceIssues E30 and the item's review note
findings.claim: The E30 repair changes M_℘ to the relative crystal but still defines W^t_℘ = Lie(ℋ^t_℘)^∨ and asserts that it has rank 2. For the absolute Cartier dual this is false whenever [F_℘:Q_p] > 1. Consequently the displayed rank-four relative Hodge exact sequence cannot have the stated left term.
findings.evidence: Main §4.1 p562 constructs H from B_p/O_{B,p}; its ℘-factor has Z_p-height 4d, d=[F_℘:Q_p]. Theorem 4.9(1), p568, makes its Lie module rank one over the unramified quadratic O_{K0}-extension of O_℘, hence rank 2 over the model. Page 569 explicitly uses the Cartier dual. Height is unchanged by absolute Cartier duality and dimensions add to height, so Lie(ℋ^t_℘)^∨ has rank 4d−2: rank 6 already at an unramified degree-two place. E30 and the item's own note state precisely this obstruction, but the replacement statement preserves the offending equality. Merely making M relative does not change the meaning of Lie of the absolute dual.
findings.fix: Define W^t_℘ to be the rank-two relative Hodge submodule of the O_℘-relative crystal. At unramified places explicitly identify it with the τ-summand of the absolute Cartier-dual differential module, not the full module. At ramified places state the required relative theory/image convention and its comparison obligation; do not assert that a raw τ-quotient is locally free. Define N from those same pieces and propagate the convention to cotangent-tensor, determinant-cancellation and comparison-line as needed. Retain the existing E3/E31 gate. This repairs propagation of E30 and does not request a second generic Dieudonné owner.

findings.claim: The test-function construction still asserts that a maximal compact U containing Ô_E^× gives a maximal order Ô_B containing Ô_E. This is exactly the inference rejected by accepted sourceIssue E28. The corrected quaternion-datum and endpoint theorems are not actually imported as the U hypothesis here: the item names only F,E,B from Theorem 1.7, then specifies U separately using the weaker condition.
findings.evidence: Main §7.2 p591 contains the inference O_{E_v}^× ⊂ U_v ⇒ O_{E_v} ⊂ O_{B_v}; E28 gives its dyadic split counterexample. Recompute it with E=Q(√−7), v=2, E_v=Q_2×Q_2 diagonally embedded in M_2(Q_2), and L={(x,y)∈Z_2²:x≡y mod2}. U_v=Aut(L) is maximal compact and contains all diagonal pairs of units. In the basis (1,1),(0,2), their lower-left entry is (d−a)/2∈Z_2. But diag(1,0) has lower-left entry −1/2, so O_{E_v} is not contained in End(L). The order generated by U_v is contained in End(L), so the parenthetical containment in test-function is false under its explicit hypothesis. Its claimed O_E-module basis and the order-sandwich inclusion need the stronger order hypothesis.
findings.fix: Make test-function consume quaternion-datum with U=Ô_B^× for a chosen maximal order Ô_B⊇Ô_E, and state that condition directly. Pass the same chosen order and integral j to order-sandwich and local computations. Remove the implication from unit-group containment in the accepted statement/review paraphrase, or mark it as the rejected printed argument. Keep E28 as the source issue; no new source-erratum record is needed.

findings.claim: The review-added height-decomposition input requires a single finite extension H/F over which every point of CM_U is defined. The paper only gives a finite extension for each point and permits finite composita. CM_U is the entire varying-conductor CM set, not the finite orbit C_U. The stronger hypothesis generally has no witness and cannot supply the height-decomposition theorem.
findings.evidence: Main §8.1 p607 gives the pointwise field-of-definition assertion, immediately followed by: 'The composite of two such extensions still satisfies the same property.' The two different sets C_U and CM_U are defined on p606 and separately in extraction item rev-cm-points-on-x-u. Under CM reciprocity the stabilizer of [β]_U is E^×(E_A,f^×∩βUβ^{-1}), so changing β allows growing local conductors. For example take F=Q, E=Q(√−7), an incoherent quaternion datum ramified at ∞,3,5, and maximal order level containing O_E. At the split place 2 the lattices L_n={(x,y)∈Z_2²:x≡y mod2^n} have multiplier order Z_2+2^n O_{E,2}. The associated ring-class orbits have unbounded degree: h(Z+2^n O_E)=2^{n−1} for n≥1 (h(O_E)=1, O_E^×={±1}, and 2 splits). Thus a fixed finite H cannot rationalize all of CM_U. This quantifier change is in the extracted item, not in the paper.
findings.fix: Choose H after the finitely many CM points/supports entering a given intersection calculation have been fixed; enlarge by a finite compositum as necessary, preserving unramifiedness above Σ(B_f). State normalized base-change independence so the coefficientwise pairings assemble to the height series. Do not demand simultaneous rationality of every point in CM_U. Distinguish this from choosing one field for the finite orbit C_U. Keep the Q-factoriality hypothesis and all S2 and normalization conditions.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18.result.json: proofOutline fields of determinant-cancellation (items[113]), local-n (items[93]), local-cancel-split (items[99]) and nonzero-theta (items[100])
findings.claim: Several accepted proof outlines still prescribe arguments that their corrected statements and appended review notes explicitly refute. These are affirmative false intermediate steps, rather than merely deferred external proofs.
findings.evidence: determinant-cancellation still instructs identifying the O_E-linear deformation Hom with the O_B-linear Hom from main pp575–576; E32 and its note show their generic ranks are respectively 2 and 1. The corrected statement instead uses cancellation of determinant twists. local-n still ends 'S2 gives zero', whereas its statement and E51 give n_φ(1,1)=−1/(1+N+N²). local-cancel-split says 2n log N cancels log|q(y)|, which is false at S2 and y=u=1: the latter is zero and the former is nonzero. E43/E51 instead cancel 2n log N against c_φ. nonzero-theta still asks for positive/nonnegative terms, whereas its statement and E52 retain a potentially negative common Weil-index sign. These contradictions are present in the machine-readable proofOutline fields even though the corrections appear in note fields.
findings.fix: Replace those outlines with the arguments already specified by the review: cancel the W(I^t)-twists directly for Corollary 5.5, retaining the ramified-base gate; distinguish S2 from its complement and use c_φ=2n_φ log N there; prove the theta constant term nonzero from a common sign and one nonzero term. Audit the other corrected items for the same stale-field pattern. Keep historical source assertions in sourceIssues, not in the current proof plan. This asks for consistency of retained outlines, not additional blueprint-level proof closure.
